title: The Equality Case of Lyapunov's Inequality
description: Pins down the equality case of Lyapunov's interpolation inequality, directly answering the first open question of the parent Lyapunov entry. The parent proves A(a·p + b·r) ≤ A(p)^a · A(r)^b for the weighted moment function A(t) = ∑_i w_i·x_i^t of a strictly positive family with convex weights a, b > 0, a + b = 1. This entry proves that for distinct exponents p ≠ r, equality holds if and only if the data x is constant: A(a·p + b·r) = A(p)^a · A(r)^b ↔ ∀ i j, x_i = x_j. Equivalently, the moment curve t ↦ log A(t) is strictly convex away from the degenerate locus where all x_i coincide (where A(t) = (∑ w_i)·c^t is genuinely log-affine). The engine is the two-variable weighted AM–GM equality case (amgm_two_weighted_eq_iff, from the grandparent two-variable Young entry), applied pointwise and summed: normalising to probability vectors S_i = w_i·x_i^p/A(p), T_i = w_i·x_i^r/A(r), the pointwise weighted AM–GM S_i^a·T_i^b ≤ a·S_i + b·T_i sums to Lyapunov's inequality, and a sum of ≤'s is an equality iff it is termwise an equality (Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le). Termwise equality S_i = T_i says x_i^{p-r} = A(p)/A(r) is the same constant for every i, which for p ≠ r forces all x_i equal by injectivity of t ↦ t^{p-r}. This deliberately avoids the (unformalised in Mathlib) general Hölder equality case: the only equality input is the two-variable AM–GM. Two corollaries are included: the strict inequality for non-constant data, and the equality case of the symmetric three-exponent form A(q)^{r-p} = A(p)^{r-q}·A(r)^{q-p} ↔ x constant for p < q < r.

meta.author: Lean Genius (equality case of Lyapunov's inequality via summed two-variable AM–GM); A. M. Lyapunov
originalContributions: moment_interp_eq_iff: the equality case of Lyapunov's interpolation inequality — for strictly positive families w, x, distinct exponents p ≠ r, and convex weights a, b > 0 with a + b = 1, equality A(a·p + b·r) = A(p)^a · A(r)^b holds iff the data x is constant (∀ i j, x_i = x_j). This directly answers open question #1 of the parent Lyapunov entry. Proved by normalising the two moment families to probability vectors and applying the two-variable weighted AM–GM equality case pointwise; equality of the resulting sum of pointwise inequalities is termwise equality, which forces x_i^{p-r} to be a fixed constant and hence (p ≠ r) all x_i equal.

normalized_amgm_sum_eq_one_iff: the abstract core — for nonnegative probability vectors u, v (∑ u = ∑ v = 1) and convex weights a, b > 0 with a + b = 1, the weighted geometric average ∑_i u_i^a·v_i^b equals 1 iff u_i = v_i for every i. This isolates the global step (a sum of pointwise AM–GM inequalities is an equality iff termwise, via Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le) from the rpow bookkeeping, and is reusable for any equality-case-of-summed-AM–GM argument.

moment_interp_lt_of_not_const: the strict Lyapunov inequality — when the data x is non-constant, A(a·p + b·r) < A(p)^a · A(r)^b. Equivalently, t ↦ log A(t) is strictly convex off the single-point locus.

moment_lyapunov_eq_iff: the equality case of the symmetric three-exponent form — for p < q < r, A(q)^{r-p} = A(p)^{r-q}·A(r)^{q-p} iff x is constant. Derived from moment_interp_eq_iff with a = (r-q)/(r-p), b = (q-p)/(r-p) by injectivity of raising to the positive power r - p.
meta.assumptions: None beyond Mathlib's foundational axioms. Fully machine-checked: 0 sorries, 0 axiom declarations, no native_decide; all theorems depend only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The file imports two other gallery entries — Proofs/JensenInequalityOQ01OQ01OQ01OQ01OQ01 (the parent Lyapunov inequality, for the moment function and the inequality moment_interp_le) and Proofs/JensenInequalityOQ01OQ01 (the grandparent two-variable Young entry, for the AM–GM equality case amgm_two_weighted_eq_iff).

crossReferences.description: Answers the parent Lyapunov entry's first open question by proving the equality case of its interpolation inequality moment_interp_le: equality A(a·p+b·r) = A(p)^a·A(r)^b holds iff all x_i are equal. The strict inequality moment_interp_lt_of_not_const is built directly on the parent's moment_interp_le.

Second-order sharpening of the equality case of the power-mean inequality (M_r = M_t iff x constant): that entry compares two points of the moment curve; this one characterises when a chord of the log-moment curve touches it, i.e. the equality case of its convexity.

overview.historicalContext: Lyapunov's inequality states that the moments of a positive measure are a log-convex function of their order. The equality case is the companion sharp statement: log-convexity is strict — the chord lies strictly above the curve — except on the degenerate locus where the underlying function is constant (a single atom), in which case the moment function A(t) = W·c^t is exactly log-affine and every chord touches the curve. This is the discrete, elementary prototype of the rigidity statements that accompany the interpolation inequalities (Hölder, Lyapunov, Riesz–Thorin): equality in the interpolation bound is a strong structural constraint forcing proportionality of the interpolated data. Mathlib provides the two-variable weighted AM–GM and its equality case but not the equality case of the general discrete Hölder inequality, so the present argument is deliberately routed through the two-variable AM–GM summed pointwise rather than through a general Hölder rigidity lemma.
overview.problemStatement: For strictly positive families w, x : ι → ℝ on a nonempty finite index type, with the weighted moment function A(t) = ∑_i w_i·x_i^t, characterise when the Lyapunov interpolation inequality A(a·p + b·r) ≤ A(p)^a·A(r)^b is an equality. Prove that for distinct exponents p ≠ r and convex weights a, b > 0 with a + b = 1, equality holds if and only if all x_i are equal; derive the strict inequality for non-constant data and the equality case of the symmetric three-exponent form.
overview.proofStrategy: Normalise the two moment families to probability vectors S_i = w_i·x_i^p/A(p) and T_i = w_i·x_i^r/A(r), so that ∑ S = ∑ T = 1. The two-variable weighted AM–GM gives the pointwise bound S_i^a·T_i^b ≤ a·S_i + b·T_i. Summing, the left side equals A(a·p+b·r)/(A(p)^a·A(r)^b) (via the interpolation identity (w·x^p)^a·(w·x^r)^b = w·x^{a·p+b·r}) and the right side equals a + b = 1, recovering Lyapunov's inequality. The abstract lemma normalized_amgm_sum_eq_one_iff records that this sum equals 1 iff it is termwise equality (Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le), with each term resolved by the AM–GM equality case amgm_two_weighted_eq_iff: S_i^a·T_i^b = a·S_i + b·T_i ↔ S_i = T_i. Termwise S_i = T_i unwinds (cancelling w_i > 0 and the positive normalisers) to x_i^p·A(r) = x_i^r·A(p), i.e. x_i^{p-r} = A(p)/A(r), the same constant for every i; for p ≠ r this forces x_i = x_j by injectivity of t ↦ t^{p-r} (Real.rpow_left_inj). The converse direction is the direct computation that constant data makes A(t) = (∑ w_i)·c^t and both sides equal (∑ w_i)·c^{a·p+b·r}. The strict inequality is lt_of_le_of_ne against the equality case, and the three-exponent equality is obtained by raising the two-exponent equality to the positive power r - p (again using injectivity of rpow in the base).
keyInsights: Equality in a summed inequality is equality termwise: the entire rigidity content is Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le, reducing the global equality case to the two-variable AM–GM equality case applied at each index.

Normalising the moment families to probability vectors is what turns the pointwise AM–GM into Lyapunov's inequality with the sharp constant 1 on the right; without normalisation the pointwise sum does not reassemble into the geometric mean A(p)^a·A(r)^b.

Termwise equality S_i = T_i is the statement that x_i^{p-r} = A(p)/A(r) is independent of i — a single equation per index whose only solution (for p ≠ r and positive data) is x_i constant, by injectivity of the base in t ↦ t^{p-r}.

The general Hölder equality case is not needed and is not in Mathlib: routing through the two-variable AM–GM summed pointwise gives the full rigidity statement from a single, already-formalised equality lemma.

The equality locus is exponent-independent: it is the same single-point locus {x constant} for every choice of p ≠ r and weights a, b, whereas the inequality itself is non-trivial for all non-constant data — mirroring how the power-mean equality locus is sign-independent even as the inequality flips across zero.

sections.title: Equality case of the interpolation inequality
sections.summary: moment_interp_eq_iff: A(a·p+b·r) = A(p)^a·A(r)^b ↔ x constant (for p ≠ r). Forward: normalise to S_i, T_i, apply the core lemma to get S_i = T_i, unwind to x_i^{p-r} = A(p)/A(r) constant, conclude x_i = x_j by Real.rpow_left_inj. conclusion.summary: This fully verified 216-line file (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide; all theorems depend only on propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound) settles the equality case of Lyapunov's inequality: for distinct exponents p ≠ r, the interpolation bound A(a·p+b·r) ≤ A(p)^a·A(r)^b is an equality iff the data x is constant. It also delivers the strict inequality for non-constant data and the equality case of the symmetric three-exponent form. The single equality input is the two-variable weighted AM–GM equality case, applied pointwise to normalised moment families and summed, with the rigidity packaged in the reusable abstract lemma normalized_amgm_sum_eq_one_iff.
conclusion.implications: The result completes the rigidity picture for the discrete Lyapunov inequality: log-convexity of moments is strict precisely off the single-point locus, so the gallery's power-mean monotonicity and power-mean equality entries are exposed as first- and second-order shadows of one convexity phenomenon. The abstract core (a summed AM–GM is an equality iff termwise) is a reusable template for the equality case of any inequality obtained by summing pointwise weighted AM–GM, including discrete Hölder and Minkowski.
openQuestions: Lift the equality case to the Lᵖ / integral setting: characterise equality in the measure-theoretic Lyapunov inequality (∫ f^t)^{u-s} = (∫ f^s)^{u-t}(∫ f^u)^{t-s} as f being a.e. constant on its support, connecting to Mathlib's interpolation infrastructure.

Derive the equality case of the general n-fold discrete Hölder inequality (the parent generalized-Hölder entry) from the same summed-AM–GM template, characterising equality as proportionality of the columns (w_i·x_{j,i}^{p_j} independent of j up to scaling).
